topic.title: Reviewing Translations Before You Commit
topic.shortdesc: How to check translated files after a job finishes and before they become part of your project.

body.p: When a translation job finishes, its translated files, the translation index, and any new deliverables are brought into your workspace as ordinary, uncommitted changes. They stay there for you to review until you commit them.

ul.li: The changed files as a set - Use the workspace Changes view to see everything the job wrote, so you can confirm it changed what you expected and nothing else. See Data Handling and Your Responsibilities for why reviewing the full set matters.

Translation quality - Open a translated topic in the visual editor and read it against the English source. Machine translation can produce fluent text that still changes the intended meaning, so read for meaning, not just for obvious errors. For ways to gain confidence in the translation, including when you do not read the target language, see Ways to Check Translation Quality.
Validation problems - Use the Problems view to confirm that the translated publication is valid DITA and does not contain broken references.

section.title: Ways to Check Translation Quality
section.p: Reading each translated topic against its source is the most direct check, but it assumes you read the target language. The following approaches help you gain confidence in a translation, including when you do not.

ul.li: Send it to a bilingual reviewer. Start a review task that contains the target-language files and assign it to a reviewer who knows both languages, attaching the English PDF for reference.

Back-translate with the agent. If you do not understand the target language, have the agent translate the content back into the source language and compare the result with the original. Because the agent keeps no memory between jobs, it reads the target-language files much as a new reader would, so a faithful round trip is a good signal that the meaning survived.
Delete the source-language folder and the publications you want to check.
Ask the agent to translate from the target language back into the source language.
Bring the result into your workspace.
Compare the back-translation against the original in the Changes view.
Ask a separate agent to review. Ask the agent to review the topics that are already translated without translating anything, and to write a Markdown report of the problems it finds.

section.title: Correcting and Committing
section.p: You can edit any translated file directly before committing; the agent reuses such corrections as context on later jobs (see Manual Edits Are Preserved as Context). When you are satisfied, commit the translated files, the index, and the deliverables together so translation state stays consistent with the content.
